# `silk/simd/f32x4`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Operations on `simd<f32, 4>`: four 32-bit float lanes in one 128-bit vector.

## When to use
Use this module to work on four `f32` values at once. Use [`load`](#load) and [`store`](#store)
to move lanes between a slice and a vector, a lane comparison such as [`lanesEqual`](#lanesEqual) to make
a `mask<4>`, and `silk.simd.mask4` to test that mask.

## Details
The operators `+`, `-`, `*`, `/` and `%` apply lane by lane and follow IEEE 754 as the
`f32` operators do. `==` is true only when every lane is equal, and a NaN lane is never
equal. [`reduceAdd`](#reduceAdd) adds lanes in order, so it gives the same result on every target.
Lane `0` is at the lowest address in memory.

## Examples
### Scale every lane and add the results
```silk
import silk.simd.f32x4

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let values = f32x4.fromArray([1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0])
  let doubled = f32x4.mulAdd(values, f32x4.splat(2.0), f32x4.splat(0.0))
  if f32x4.reduceAdd(doubled) != 20.0 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

Import as `f32x4` with `import silk.simd.f32x4 as f32x4`.

<a id="load"></a>

## `load`

```silk
pub fn load(lanes: &[f32], offset: usize) -> simd<f32, 4>
```

Reads [`LANES`](#LANES) lanes of `lanes` starting at `offset`.

### Gotchas
Traps unless `offset + LANES` is at most `lanes.length`. The slice needs no alignment beyond
`f32`.

## `store`

```silk
pub fn store(lanes: &mut [f32], offset: usize, vector: simd<f32, 4>) -> ()
```

Writes the lanes of `vector` into `lanes` starting at `offset`.

### Gotchas
Traps unless `offset + LANES` is at most `lanes.length`.

<a id="loadUnchecked"></a>

## `loadUnchecked`

```silk
pub unsafe fn loadUnchecked(pointer: [*]const f32) -> simd<f32, 4>
```

Reads [`LANES`](#LANES) lanes starting at `pointer`, with no bounds check.

### Gotchas
The caller proves that `pointer` addresses [`LANES`](#LANES) live lanes aligned to `f32`.

<a id="minimum"></a>

## `minimum`

```silk
pub fn minimum(left: simd<f32, 4>, right: simd<f32, 4>) -> simd<f32, 4>
```

Returns the smaller lane of each pair. A NaN lane in either input gives NaN, and `-0.0` is
less than `0.0`.

<a id="shuffle"></a>

## `shuffle`

```silk
pub fn shuffle(left: simd<f32, 4>, right: simd<f32, 4>, static indices: [usize; 4]) -> simd<f32, 4>
```

Returns a vector whose lane `i` is lane `indices[i]` of `left` followed by `right`.

### Details
An index below [`LANES`](#LANES) selects from `left`, and an index from [`LANES`](#LANES) to `2 * LANES - 1`
selects from `right`. The indices are static, so each call is one fixed lane permutation.

```silk
pub fn reduceAdd(vector: simd<f32, 4>) -> f32
```

<a id="reduceAddUnordered"></a>

## `reduceAddUnordered`

```silk
pub fn reduceAddUnordered(vector: simd<f32, 4>) -> f32
```

Returns the sum of every lane, added in the order the target prefers.

### Gotchas
The rounding can differ between targets. Use [`reduceAdd`](#reduceAdd) for a result that is the same
everywhere.
